explanation: Paging is a memory management technique that divides the virtual address space into fixed-size blocks called pages and maps them to non-contiguous blocks in physical memory called page frames. It is used to provide efficient memory utilization, support for virtual memory, and flexibility in memory allocation without requiring contiguous physical space, allowing the OS to manage memory more effectively and handle processes independently of their memory usage patterns.
example_explanation: This program demonstrates paging by using an array as a page table to map a virtual page (index 0) to a physical frame (value 3). It shows how a simple mapping can simulate the core idea of paging, where virtual addresses are translated to physical ones, illustrating the abstraction and flexibility of memory management in a minimal way.
